papers.title: Red Teaming Language Models with Language Models
papers.abstract: Introduced the concept of using language models to automatically discover adversarial prompts, significantly advancing jailbreaking techniques.

papers.title: Jailbroken: How Does LLM Safety Training Fail?
papers.abstract: Introduced the concept of jailbroken language models, demonstrating how safety training can fail.

papers.title: Do Anything Now: Characterizing and Evaluating In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts on LLMs
papers.abstract: Characterized and evaluated in-the-wild jailbreak prompts on LLMs, providing insights into the effectiveness of jailbreak prompts.

papers.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
papers.abstract: Introduced the concept of universal adversarial suffixes that could jailbreak multiple aligned language models simultaneously.

papers.title: Jailbreaking Black Box LLMs in Twenty Queries
papers.abstract: Demonstrated efficient black-box jailbreaking methods that could bypass safety measures with minimal queries.

papers.title: Tree of Attacks: Jailbreaking Black-Box LLMs Automatically
papers.abstract: Introduced Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP), an automated method for generating jailbreaks that only requires black-box access to the target LLM, achieving over 80% success rate on state-of-the-art LLMs.

papers.title: AutoDAN: Generating Stealthy Jailbreak Prompts on Aligned Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Introduced AutoDAN, a hierarchical genetic algorithm that automatically generates stealthy jailbreak prompts while preserving semantic meaningfulness and bypassing perplexity-based defenses.

papers.title: Baseline Defenses for Adversarial Attacks Against Aligned Language Models
papers.abstract: Proposed defense mechanisms against jailbreaking attacks, including perplexity filtering and adversarial training.

papers.title: SmoothLLM: Defending Large Language Models Against Jailbreaking Attacks
papers.abstract: Proposed a novel defense mechanism that uses randomized smoothing to make language models robust against jailbreaking attacks.

papers.title: HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal
papers.abstract: Introduced a standardized evaluation framework for automated red teaming and robust refusal, providing a benchmark for evaluating the robustness of LLMs.

papers.title: JailbreakBench: An Open Benchmark for Jailbreaking LLMs
papers.abstract: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating jailbreaking attacks and defenses across multiple LLMs.

papers.title: Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks
papers.abstract: Introduced a simple adaptive attack that can jailbreak leading safety-aligned LLMs.

papers.title: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers
papers.abstract: Proposed the circuit breaker defense that uses representation engineering to fine-tune LLMs to be more robust against jailbreaking attacks.

papers.title: Many-Shot Jailbreaking
papers.abstract: Introduced many-shot jailbreaking, a technique that leverages large numbers of examples to bypass safety measures in language models.

papers.title: Constitutional Classifiers: Defending against Universal Jailbreaks across Thousands of Hours of Red Teaming
papers.abstract: Introduced Constitutional Classifiers, safeguards trained on synthetic data generated by prompting LLMs with natural language rules to defend against universal jailbreaks while maintaining deployment viability.

papers.title: Latent Adversarial Training Improves Robustness to Persistent Harmful Behaviors in LLMs
papers.abstract: Introduced targeted latent adversarial training (LAT) to improve robustness to jailbreaks, remove backdoors without trigger knowledge, and unlearn undesirable knowledge more effectively than existing methods.

papers.title: AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Introduced AgentHarm, a benchmark containing malicious agent tasks covering eleven harm categories to evaluate LLM agent misuse and jailbreaking effectiveness.

papers.title: StrongREJECT: Jailbreaking Large Language Models in Few Queries via Strong Rejection
papers.abstract: Introduced StrongREJECT, a benchmark to evaluate the harmfulness and specificity of responses returned by jailbroken LLMs.

papers.title: Jailbreaking LLM-Controlled Robots
papers.abstract: Demonstrated that robots controlled by LLMs can be jailbroken to perform dangerous actions in the physical world.

papers.title: Deliberative Alignment: Reasoning Enables Safer Language Models
papers.abstract: Introduced deliberative alignment, a paradigm that teaches models safety specifications and trains them to reason over these specifications before answering.

papers.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
papers.abstract: Proposed an instruction hierarchy that explicitly defines how models should behave when instructions of different priorities conflict, teaching LLMs to selectively ignore lower-privileged instructions.

papers.title: Benchmarking Misuse Mitigation Against Covert Adversaries
papers.abstract: Introduced a benchmark for evaluating misuse mitigation against covert adversaries, providing insights into the effectiveness of misuse mitigation techniques.
